subproblems.title: A nonempty embedded d-dimensional submanifold of ℝ^P has d ≤ P (Simon Ch. 2, §4)
subproblems.statement: Let P, d, r ∈ ℕ and M ⊆ ℝ^P (Euclid P). Assume IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r d M: for every y ∈ M there are an open V ⊆ ℝ^d, an open W ⊆ ℝ^P with y ∈ W, and ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P such that ψ is Cʳ on V, injective on V and proper (V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W), ψ(V) = W ∩ M, and Dψ(z) = fderiv ℝ ψ z is injective for every z ∈ V. If M is nonempty, then d ≤ P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d r : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)), IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r d M → M.Nonempty → d ≤ P
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Step 1 of the parent proof (n + 1 ≤ P), stated for an arbitrary nonempty embedded submanifold; Simon Ch. 2, §4, (4.1) (chapter-02.txt lines 849–856: a 1:1 Cʳ map ψ : V → W with ψ(V) = W ∩ M, ψ proper, Dψ of maximal rank on V). The parent applies it with d := n + 1, r := 2, M := N. This is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration Submission.regcomp_cop_dim_le_of_embedded, reused with its identical frozen type.

Proof. Fix P, d, r ∈ ℕ and M ⊆ ℝ^P with IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r d M and M ≠ ∅.
1. Since M is nonempty, choose y ∈ M.
2. Apply IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r d M at y. It yields V ⊆ ℝ^d, W ⊆ ℝ^P and ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P with y ∈ W, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, and Dψ(z) = fderiv ℝ ψ z : ℝ^d → ℝ^P injective for every z ∈ V. The other chart properties (V and W open, ψ of class Cʳ on V, ψ injective on V, ψ proper) are not used.
3. Since y ∈ W and y ∈ M, we have y ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V). Hence there is z ∈ V with ψ(z) = y.
4. L := Dψ(z) is a continuous ℝ-linear map ℝ^d → ℝ^P. As an ℝ-linear map it has the same underlying function, so it is injective by step 2, because z ∈ V. An injective linear map into a finite-dimensional space cannot raise dimension, so finrank ℝ^d ≤ finrank ℝ^P (Mathlib LinearMap.finrank_le_finrank_of_injective; ℝ^P is finite-dimensional).
5. For every q, finrank ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q)) = q (Mathlib finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). With q = d and q = P, step 4 reads d ≤ P. ∎
proof_key_steps: Pick y ∈ M and a chart (V, W, ψ) of M at y with ψ(V) = W ∩ M and Dψ injective on V.
y ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V) gives a point z ∈ V.
Dψ(z) : ℝ^d → ℝ^P is an injective linear map, so d = finrank ℝ^d ≤ finrank ℝ^P = P.

subproblems.title: The boundary of a region in N is supported in N (Simon 7.5.1 and Ch. 6, 2.11)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U, N, E ⊆ ℝ^P, ξ_N : ℝ^P → Λ_{n+1}(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P (n+1)) and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n). Assume U is open, (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, E ⊆ N, and T(ω) = ∫_E ξ_N(x)(dω(x)) dH^{n+1}(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξ_N, H^{n+1} = μHE[n+1]). Then spt T ⊆ N. Here spt T = U ∖ Z(T), and Z(T) is the union of all open W with closure W compact and contained in U such that T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W (GeometricCurrentOn.support).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U N E : Set (Euclid P)) (ξN : Euclid P → MultiVector P (n + 1)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → (closure N \ N) ∩ U = ∅ → E ⊆ N → IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξN → T.support ⊆ N
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Step 2 of the parent proof (spt T ⊆ U ∩ N), with only the hypotheses it uses: Simon 7.5.1 (T = ∂[[E]] in U with E ⊆ N; chapter-07.txt lines 746–756) and Simon Ch. 6, 2.11 (definition of spt T; chapter-06.txt lines 297–301). The inclusion spt T ⊆ U holds by definition and is added by the parent. This is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration Submission.regcomp_cop_region_support_subset, reused with its identical frozen type.

Notation. tsupport ω is the closed support of a form ω. For ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), dω is its exterior derivative (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative), and tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω (SimonGMT tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset). Z(T) and spt T = U ∖ Z(T) are as in the statement (GeometricCurrentOn.zeroRegion, GeometricCurrentOn.support).

Proof. Fix the data and hypotheses, and let x ∈ spt T. We show x ∈ N.
1. By definition of spt T, x ∈ U and x ∉ Z(T). Suppose, for a contradiction, that x ∉ N.
2. Then x ∉ closure N. Otherwise x ∈ (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U, which is empty by hypothesis.
3. U ∖ closure N is open, because U is open and closure N is closed. By steps 1 and 2 it contains x. Choose r > 0 with B_r(x) ⊆ U ∖ closure N, and put W₀ := B_{r/2}(x).
4. W₀ is open. Its closure lies in closedBall(x, r/2), which is compact because closed balls of ℝ^P are compact. So closure W₀ is compact, being a closed subset of a compact set. Moreover closedBall(x, r/2) ⊆ B_r(x) ⊆ U, so closure W₀ ⊆ U.
5. T vanishes on W₀. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W₀. Then tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W₀ ⊆ B_r(x). Let z ∈ E. Then z ∈ N ⊆ closure N. Since B_r(x) ∩ closure N = ∅, z ∉ B_r(x), so z ∉ tsupport dω and dω(z) = 0. As ξ_N(z) is linear, ξ_N(z)(dω(z)) = ξ_N(z)(0) = 0. So the integrand of T(ω) = ∫_E ξ_N(z)(dω(z)) dH^{n+1}(z) (IsBoundaryOfRegion) vanishes at every point of E, and T(ω) = 0. A set integral of a function that vanishes at every point of the integration set is 0, with no measurability assumption on E (Mathlib setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero).
6. By steps 4 and 5, W₀ is one of the sets whose union is Z(T). Since x ∈ W₀, x ∈ Z(T), which contradicts step 1. Hence x ∈ N.
Therefore spt T ⊆ N. ∎
proof_key_steps: A point x ∈ spt T ∖ N lies in U and, because (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, outside closure N.
Choose B_r(x) ⊆ U ∖ closure N; then W₀ = B_{r/2}(x) is open with compact closure contained in U.
If tsupport ω ⊆ W₀, then tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω misses E ⊆ N, so the integrand ξ_N(dω) vanishes on E and T(ω) = 0.
Hence x ∈ W₀ ⊆ Z(T), contradicting x ∈ spt T = U ∖ Z(T); so spt T ⊆ N.

subproblems.title: The boundary of a region is a cycle, ∂(∂[[E]]) = 0 (Simon 7.5.1, 6.1.12, 6.2.3)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, E ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets, ξ_N : ℝ^P → Λ_{n+1}(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P (n+1)) and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n). If T(ω) = ∫_E ξ_N(x)(dω(x)) dH^{n+1}(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξ_N, H^{n+1} = μHE[n+1]), then ∂T = 0 in U. This is BoundaryVanishes T: True by convention when n = 0, and T.boundary = 0 when n = m + 1, where T.boundary(φ) = T(dφ) for φ ∈ 𝒟^m(U).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U E : Set (Euclid P)) (ξN : Euclid P → MultiVector P (n + 1)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξN → BoundaryVanishes T
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Step 3 of the parent proof (∂T = 0), stated with only the hypothesis it uses: Simon 7.5.1 (T = ∂[[E]]; chapter-07.txt lines 746–756), Ch. 6 (1.12) d²ω = 0 (chapter-06.txt line 150), and Ch. 6 (2.3) ∂T(ω) = T(dω) with ∂T = 0 if n = 0 (chapter-06.txt lines 216–220). No hypothesis on U, E or ξ_N is needed. This is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration Submission.regcomp_cop_region_boundary_vanishes, reused with its identical frozen type.

Proof. Fix the data and assume IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξ_N.
1. If n = 0, BoundaryVanishes T is True by definition (Simon's convention ∂T = 0 for 0-currents). There is nothing to prove.
2. Let n = m + 1; we show T.boundary = 0. Currents in U that agree on every test form are equal (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), so fix φ ∈ 𝒟^m(U). By the definition of the boundary (6.2.3; GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply), ∂T(φ) = T(dφ). Here dφ ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U) is the exterior derivative of φ as a test form in U (exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m φ): it is smooth and compactly supported, with tsupport dφ ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ U.
3. The hypothesis applied to the test form dφ gives T(dφ) = ∫_E ξ_N(x)(d(dφ)(x)) dH^{m+2}(x).
4. Since φ is smooth, d(dφ) = 0 (Simon (6.1.12); SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_sq). So for every x, ξ_N(x)(d(dφ)(x)) = ξ_N(x)(0) = 0 by linearity of ξ_N(x). The integral in step 3 is therefore the integral of the zero function, which is 0.
5. Hence ∂T(φ) = 0 = 0(φ) for every φ ∈ 𝒟^m(U), so T.boundary = 0. This is BoundaryVanishes T for n = m + 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: For n = 0, BoundaryVanishes T is True by definition.
For n = m + 1 and φ ∈ 𝒟^m(U), ∂T(φ) = T(dφ) = ∫_E ξ_N(d(dφ)) dH^{m+2}.
d(dφ) = 0 for smooth φ, so the integrand ξ_N(x)(0) = 0 and the integral vanish; T.boundary = 0 by extensionality.
